A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OpenEarthAgent work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained material to be matched across restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original step-by-step and end-to-end experiments in Tables 3–4, model-selection experiments, error analysis, and qualitative demonstrations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds ablations, external-benchmark evaluation, domain-specific analysis, and a judge comparison.

M1.justification: v1 Section 4 and v3 Section 3.2 retain the same tool registry, orchestrator, cache, replay validation, and masked maximum-likelihood objective. The new ablations test variants of existing components; benchmark interface formatting does not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 Supplement S2 adds evaluation on the separate Earth-Agent benchmark, described as 248 tasks with 13,729 images spanning spectrum, products, and RGB modalities. The original 14,538 training and 1,169 evaluation instances remain unchanged. The new domain breakdown stratifies existing coverage rather than adding domains.

E2.justification: GPT-5 joins the corresponding step-by-step and end-to-end comparisons in Tables 3–4 and Figures 6–7, with previous comparators retained. New Table A2 also compares OpenEarthAgent against Qwen3 with 5, 10, and 15 in-context demonstrations, substantially extending comparison beyond the original instruction-only baselines.

E3.justification: The original training recipe and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. New experiments introduce easy/hard training subsets, varying demonstration counts, five tool schemas, three tool-order configurations, and planning controls. External-benchmark testing uses reformatted tool interfaces, while S8.1 substitutes Qwen3-30B for the original judge under the same scoring prompt.

E4.justification: New Tables A1–A5 examine data composition, in-context learning, schema information, tool ordering, and high-level planning. New Figures A2 and A6 analyze domain-specific performance and judge sensitivity. The earlier model-selection study, error analysis, and qualitative cases are retained rather than replaced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new judge comparison reports alternative scores and ranking consistency without introducing statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds GPT-5 results, ablation outcomes, external-benchmark scores, and domain and judge comparisons. Existing rows in Tables 3–4 and the model-selection table are unchanged, including OpenEarthAgent's 45.26 answer accuracy. Newly reported Earth-Agent results include 96.91 instance accuracy and 70.33 tool accuracy; these concern different evaluation data, not an improvement over the original scores.

T1.justification: The tool-schema definition, trajectory formulation, and training objective in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: v3 foregrounds the executable registry and deterministic validation in the abstract and contribution list. Its conclusion also softens v1's categorical assertion that advanced benchmarks and training frameworks are absent. The central task, corpus contribution, supervised-learning approach, and competitive-performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations of mixed-trajectory training, schema grounding, planning, tool ordering, and cross-benchmark performance. It discusses diminishing returns from additional demonstrations, reduced operational flexibility under ordering rules, domain-specific difficulty, and judge leniency with preserved rankings. These interpretations substantially extend the earlier discussion.

D1.justification: v3 documents how demonstrations enter conversational history, details schema-conditioning variants, and describes external-benchmark tool reformatting. It adds a future code/model release statement without documenting an actual release. Core hardware, training hyperparameters, context length, and the tool I/O catalogue are retained.

R1.justification: The same 51 cited works and substantially the same related-work discussion remain. A new introduction passage contrasts the work with benchmarks emphasizing data scale and positions its contribution around coupling data, execution, and trajectory learning.

P1.justification: v3 revises the abstract and selected introductory, methodological, results, and concluding passages; fixes the unresolved table reference and duplicated batch-size sentence; and groups dataset curation and methodology under OpenEarthAgent. The appendix is reordered, but much of the original explanatory prose and narrative sequence remains.

P2.justification: v3 adds six appendix tables, a domain heatmap, a judge-comparison plot, and a category-distribution panel in Figure 4. Tables 3–4 and Figures 6–7 accommodate GPT-5, Figure 3 is reformatted, and table captions move above tables. Retained supplementary displays are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important gaps in v1's evidence through component ablations, prompting alternatives, an independent benchmark, and domain and judge checks. These substantially improve support for design choices and clarify performance sensitivity. External-benchmark evidence remains step-by-step only, and Figure A6 supports ranking stability more strongly than absolute-score reliability, but these limits do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
